if [ -z "$FORTRESS_HOME" ]; then
  cmd=$0
  emptyifslash=${cmd##*/*}
  # if the command contains any slashes at all
  if [ -z "$emptyifslash" ]; then
    # slash occurs in name, use as is
    true;
  else
    # no slash
    cmd="`which $cmd`"
  fi
  # if the command that we found resolves to a symbolic link, try to follow
  # (not possible on Solaris, yet)
  if [ -L $cmd ]; then
     READLINK=""
     if [ -e /bin/readlink ]; then
        # Linux
        READLINK=/bin/readlink
     elif [ -e /usr/bin/readlink ]; then
        # MacOS
        READLINK=/usr/bin/readlink
     else
       echo "You need to set FORTRESS_HOME to the directory containing ProjectFortress"
       echo "The target of the symbolic link could not be followed."
       exit 1
     fi
     # Follow the link, figure out if it is absolute or relative.
     target="`$READLINK $cmd`"
     emptyifslash=${target##/*}
     # if absolute (begins with /)
     if [ -z "$emptyifslash" ]; then
       cmd=$target
     else
       cmd=${cmd%/*}/$target
     fi
     # echo Symlink resolves to $cmd
  fi
  FORTRESS_HOME="${cmd%/*}/.."
  FORTRESS_HOME="`cd "$FORTRESS_HOME"; pwd`"
  echo "Guessing FORTRESS_HOME=$FORTRESS_HOME" 1>&2
fi

if [ -e "${FORTRESS_HOME}/ProjectFortress" ]; then
  true
else
  echo "FORTRESS_HOME should be the name of the parent directory of ProjectFortress"
  echo "instead of '$FORTRESS_HOME'"
  exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
# seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
#
# Makes a worktree that is ready to compile and run Fortress without building anything, by copying the
# build and the caches of a baseline worktree that has been built once, and translating the parts of the
# caches that are keyed by the source tree's absolute path (explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md).
#
#   <base-worktree>  a clean worktree of this repository at some commit B, on which `ant compileAll`, the
#                    restore of default_repository/caches/global.map and the library-order recompile
#                    (explorations/repo-internals.md, "Compile order matters") have run, and nothing since.
#   <new-worktree>   where the new worktree goes; made by `git worktree add`, reused if it already exists.
#   <branch>         the branch it checks out: an existing local branch, else origin's, else a new branch
#                    cut from <start-point>, which defaults to B; `-` makes a detached worktree at
#                    <start-point> instead (a skeptic's or a repair's copy of the base, for old-against-new runs).
#
# What it does, in order: adds the worktree; copies ProjectFortress/build, ProjectFortress/.dependencies
# and default_repository/caches from the base; renames every file of the AST caches (analyzed_cache,
# interpreter_cache, interpreter_parsed_cache) to the hash of its source's new path (NamingCzar.deCaseName,
# compiler/NamingCzar.java:244-245; GraphNode.java:33 hashes the canonical path) and rewrites the base path
# inside it; rewrites the base path in the bytecode-cache jars' SourceFile attributes (debug information
# only: jars copied unchanged also run, but their stack traces would name the base's files); stamps every
# copied file with one time after the checkout, because the repository uses a cached entry only when it is
# not older than its source (repository/GraphRepository.java:244, :283); and, where the new worktree's
# files differ from B, stamps the differing library sources later still, so that the next `fortress compile`
# of each rebuilds it (a changed api also makes everything that imports it stale, GraphRepository.java:600-620).
# A worktree whose ProjectFortress/src differs from B is seeded too, with a warning: the copied build is B's,
# so the worker runs ant compileAll (which deletes the caches, build.xml:715 and :356) and the library-order
# recompile before its first compiled run.
#
# A worktree that already has ProjectFortress/build is left alone (a relaunch keeps the worker's own build);
# SEED_FORCE=1 replaces its build and caches with the base's.
#
# Prints one line per step with its time, and the seeded worktree's path last. Exits non-zero, having
# removed nothing, if the base is not built or not clean. Never touches the base or the main tree.
# Run it from anywhere; it needs bash, git, python3, realpath and GNU touch.
set -euo pipefail

BASE_ARG=${1:?usage: seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]}
NEW_ARG=${2:?new worktree path}
BRANCH=${3:?branch}
BASE=$(realpath "$BASE_ARG")
step () { local now; now=$(date +%s.%N); printf '%-34s %5.1f s\n' "$1" "$(echo "$now - $T" | bc)"; T=$now; }
T=$(date +%s.%N); T_START=$T

# The base must be built and clean, or its caches do not describe its commit.
for f in ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress/Shell.class \
         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar \
         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerLibrary.jar \
         default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/CompilerSystem.jar ; do
    [ -e "$BASE/$f" ] || { echo "seed-worktree: $BASE is not built: $f is missing" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
done
if [ -n "$(git -C "$BASE" status --porcelain -- ProjectFortress Library default_repository)" ]; then
    echo "seed-worktree: $BASE has changes under ProjectFortress, Library or default_repository:" >&2
    git -C "$BASE" status --short -- ProjectFortress Library default_repository | head -5 >&2
    exit 2
fi
B=$(git -C "$BASE" rev-parse HEAD)
START=${4:-$B}

# The worktree: the same command the batch workflow's shared prefix uses, with the base commit as default.
if [ "$BRANCH" = - ]; then
    [ -d "$NEW_ARG" ] || git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q --detach "$NEW_ARG" "$START"
else
    git -C "$BASE" fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if [ ! -d "$NEW_ARG" ]; then
    git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q "$NEW_ARG" "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null \
      || git -C "$BASE" worktree add -q -b "$BRANCH" "$NEW_ARG" "$START"
fi
NEW=$(realpath "$NEW_ARG")
[ "$NEW" != "$BASE" ] || { echo "seed-worktree: the new worktree is the base" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
if [ -d "$NEW/ProjectFortress/build" ] && [ -z "${SEED_FORCE:-}" ]; then
    echo "seed-worktree: $NEW already has a build; left as it is (SEED_FORCE=1 replaces it)"
    echo "$NEW" ; exit 0
fi
mkdir -p "$NEW/tmp"
step "worktree $(git -C "$NEW" rev-parse --short HEAD)"

# The build: plain copies; nothing in it holds the base's path but scalac-compileAll.args, which
# ant compileAll writes afresh. A symlink would send every cache lookup to the base
# (explorations/coordinator/batched-climb-review.md, finding 2), so copy.
rm -rf "$NEW/ProjectFortress/build" "$NEW/ProjectFortress/.dependencies"
cp -a "$BASE/ProjectFortress/build" "$NEW/ProjectFortress/build"
[ -d "$BASE/ProjectFortress/.dependencies" ] && cp -a "$BASE/ProjectFortress/.dependencies" "$NEW/ProjectFortress/.dependencies"
rm -f "$NEW/ProjectFortress/build/scalac-compileAll.args"
step "copy ProjectFortress/build"

# The caches: everything but logs/, whose subdirectories spell the base's path.
C="$NEW/default_repository/caches"
rm -rf "$C" ; mkdir -p "$C"
for d in "$BASE"/default_repository/caches/* ; do
    [ "$(basename "$d")" = logs ] && continue
    cp -a "$d" "$C/"
done
step "copy default_repository/caches"

# Translate: the AST caches' names and texts, and the jars' class constants.
python3 - "$BASE" "$NEW" "$C" <<'PY'
import os, sys, re, struct, zipfile, shutil
base, new, caches = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
def jhash(s):                      # java.lang.String.hashCode() & 0x7fffffff, as NamingCzar.deCaseName uses it
    u = s.encode('utf-16-be'); h = 0
    for j in range(0, len(u), 2):           # over UTF-16 code units, as Java counts them
        h = (31 * h + (u[j] << 8 | u[j+1])) & 0xffffffff
    return h & 0x7fffffff
# old hash -> new hash, for every Fortress source under the base (GraphNode.java:33 hashes the canonical path)
remap = {}
for root, dirs, files in os.walk(base):
    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in ('.git', 'tmp', 'build', 'default_repository')]
    for f in files:
        if f.endswith(('.fss', '.fsi')):
            p = os.path.join(root, f)
            remap['%x' % jhash(p)] = '%x' % jhash(new + p[len(base):])
# the path is in every span (@"<path>":l:c) and in generated names (*underscore_<path>:l:c)
old_q, new_q = (base + '/').encode(), (new + '/').encode()
renamed = rewritten = kept = 0
# analyzed_cache, interpreter_cache and interpreter_parsed_cache name and fill their files the same way
for root, dirs, files in os.walk(caches):
    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in ('bytecode_cache', 'nativewrapper_cache')]
    for f in files:
        if not f.endswith(('.tfi', '.tfs')): continue
        m = re.match(r'^(.*)-([0-9a-f]+)(\.tf[is])$', f)
        p = os.path.join(root, f)
        data = open(p, 'rb').read()
        if old_q in data:
            open(p, 'wb').write(data.replace(old_q, new_q)); rewritten += 1
        if m and m.group(2) in remap:
            os.rename(p, os.path.join(root, m.group(1) + '-' + remap[m.group(2)] + m.group(3))); renamed += 1
        else:
            kept += 1
# Jars: every CONSTANT_Utf8 holding the base path, the SourceFile attribute among them, gets the new path.
# Constants are reached by index, never by byte offset, so changing a constant's length is safe.
old_p, new_p = (base + '/').encode(), (new + '/').encode()
def fix_class(b):
    n = struct.unpack('>H', b[8:10])[0]
    out = [b[:10]]; i = 10; k = 1; changed = 0
    while k < n:
        tag = b[i]
        if tag == 1:
            ln = struct.unpack('>H', b[i+1:i+3])[0]; s = b[i+3:i+3+ln]
            if old_p in s:
                s = s.replace(old_p, new_p); changed += 1
            out.append(bytes([1]) + struct.pack('>H', len(s)) + s); i += 3 + ln; k += 1
            continue
        size = {3: 4, 4: 4, 5: 8, 6: 8, 7: 2, 8: 2, 16: 2, 19: 2, 20: 2, 9: 4, 10: 4, 11: 4, 12: 4,
                15: 3, 17: 4, 18: 4}[tag]
        out.append(b[i:i+1+size]); i += 1 + size; k += 2 if tag in (5, 6) else 1
    out.append(b[i:])
    return b''.join(out), changed
consts = 0
bc = os.path.join(caches, 'bytecode_cache')
for f in sorted(os.listdir(bc)) if os.path.isdir(bc) else []:
    if not f.endswith('.jar'): continue
    p = os.path.join(bc, f); tmp = p + '.seed'
    with zipfile.ZipFile(p) as zin, zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, 'w') as zout:
        for info in zin.infolist():
            data = zin.read(info)
            if info.filename.endswith('.class') and old_p in data:
                data, c = fix_class(data); consts += c
            zout.writestr(info, data)
    shutil.copystat(p, tmp); os.replace(tmp, p)
print('ast caches: %d renamed, %d kept, %d rewritten; jars: %d constants rewritten' % (renamed, kept, rewritten, consts))
PY
step "translate paths"

# One stamp after the checkout for everything copied, so each cached entry is as new as its source:
# nanoseconds, since a stamp truncated to the second can fall before the checkout's own writes.
STAMP=$(date +%s.%N)
STAMPED=("$NEW/ProjectFortress/build" "$C")
[ -d "$NEW/ProjectFortress/.dependencies" ] && STAMPED+=("$NEW/ProjectFortress/.dependencies")
find "${STAMPED[@]}" -print0 | xargs -0 touch -h -c -d "@$STAMP"
git -C "$NEW" checkout -q -- default_repository/caches/global.map
# Library sources that differ from the base's commit, committed or not, are made newer than the cache.
CHANGED_LIB=$(git -C "$NEW" diff --name-only --diff-filter=d "$B" -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin | grep '\.fs[si]$' || true)
if [ -n "$CHANGED_LIB" ]; then
    ( cd "$NEW" && echo "$CHANGED_LIB" | xargs touch -d "@$(echo "$STAMP + 2" | bc)" )

# Sharing one build between worktrees

Machine for every timing below: nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz (2100 MHz), JDK 25.0.4, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`. The baseline build ran at load 2.5 rising to 4.8 (the batch 8 microGPT walk runs were still going until 20:41 UTC); everything after it at load 0.4 to 2.4. Worktrees: `fortress-seedbase` (built from main `7266ed23c`), and copies seeded from it.

## 1. A built tree can be copied to another path, with nothing rebuilt

The base: `ant compileAll` 82 s, then the library order 112 s (AnyType 17, CompilerBuiltin 63, CompilerLibrary 27, CompilerAlgebra 2, CompilerSystem 2), 194 s in all.

What holds the tree's path, and what the copy does with it:

- `ProjectFortress/build` holds no path but `scalac-compileAll.args`, which every `ant compileAll` rewrites. Copied as is.
- The three AST caches, `analyzed_cache/` (with `depends/`), `interpreter_cache/` and `interpreter_parsed_cache/`, name each file `<Api>-<hex of the source's canonical path hash>` (`compiler/NamingCzar.java:244-245`; the path is `getCanonicalPath()`, `repository/graph/GraphNode.java:33`), and carry the path in every span (`@"/home/user/…/AnyType.fsi":12:1~16:2`) and in generated names (`*underscore_/home/user/…/NativeArray.fss:29:30`). The copy renames each file to the hash of the new path and replaces `<base>/` by `<new>/` in its text. The foreign-Java entry `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers-d13bcf6.tfi` hashes the string `ForeignJava` (`GraphRepository.java:228`) and keeps its name.
- The bytecode-cache jars carry the path only in their classes' `SourceFile` attributes: all 397 path constants of the five library jars are that attribute, and no `.xlation` entry holds a path. Jars copied unchanged run (EqualityRung1 `PASS`, Compiled10 `pass`, `junit.sh` `OK (2 tests)`); the copy rewrites the attribute anyway (0.2 s), so stack traces name the worktree's own files.
- `nativewrapper_cache/` and `global.map` hold no path. `logs/` holds only empty directories spelling the base's path, and is not copied.
- Dates: a cached entry is used only when its file is not older than its source (`GraphRepository.java:243-244`, `:282-283`; the date is the `.tfi`/`.tfs` file's own, `CacheBasedRepository.java:160-162`), and checkout stamps every source with the checkout time. The copy stamps every copied file with one time taken after the checkout, to the nanosecond: a stamp truncated to the second fell 0.85 s before the checkout's last write in the first trial, which would have made the whole cache stale.

Measured on a copy seeded from the base (the probe script ran the same commands in both trees):

- Seeding took 2 to 3 s: `git worktree add` 0.7 to 2.1 s, the build copy 0.1 to 0.7 s, the caches 0.1 s, the translation 0.2 to 0.3 s, the stamps 0.1 to 0.4 s. A seeded worktree is 206 MB (build 40 MB, caches 36 MB).
- The library order on the copy took 0.8, 2.8, 1.3, 0.7 and 1.0 s and rewrote no cache file but the foreign-Java `.tfi` and the 20 `nativewrapper_cache` classes, which every compile rewrites in the base as well.
- Same results as the base: `fortress compile` and `fortress run` of Compiled10, Compiled9.AsString and EqualityRung1 (`pass`, `O`, `PASS`); `junit.sh` on Compiled10.test, AsString.test and EqualityRung1.test; `harness-one.sh` on BooleanOps, IntegerOrderNumerals and chain2 (`OK (3 tests)`). Outputs identical once timings and the shuffle seed are removed.
- Walk: the copy took the base's walk caches too. `explorations/claude_demo.fss` ran in 4.0 s on the copy against 15.2 s for the first run in the base. On main `7266ed23c` it fails the same way in both trees, `Unification error: Closure/Constructor for join param 1 (a:BOTTOM) got arg 98: ZZ32` at `Library/RangeInternals.fss:998`, so CLAUDE.md's walk smoke test is red today.
- Nothing in the copy reads the base or the main tree. Under `strace -f -e trace=%file`, a library compile, a program compile, a run, a walk run and a `junit.sh` run made 0 accesses to the base's path. The only main-tree paths were `/home/user/fortress/.git/…` (the copy's own git metadata, which every worktree reads), and only in the `junit.sh` run, which calls git.

The fallback the brief asked for, building every worktree in parallel at the start, was not needed and was not measured.

## 2. How Fortress notices edits

Each case was run on a seeded copy, with a snapshot of the cache before and after.

Compiler path, a library component:

- Compiling a program never rebuilds a library component. An edit to the body in `CompilerLibrary.fss` (`"v1"` to `"v2"`) followed by `fortress compile` and `fortress run` of the program printed `v1`, and no cache file changed. An api edit (a new function added to `CompilerLibrary.fsi` and `.fss`) followed by the program's compile re-analysed `CompilerLibrary.tfi` but not its component, and the run died with `NoSuchMethodError: 'fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String fortress.CompilerLibrary.seedProbe()'`.
- `fortress compile ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss` alone (24 to 25 s) rewrote its `.tfs`, its `depends/` entry and its jar. The program then printed the new value without being recompiled.
- After an edit to a `.fss` alone, nothing else is stale. After an api edit, everything that depends on that api goes stale (`GraphRepository.java:614`, by date, through every dependence). Every api and every component also depends on the root apis: CompilerLibrary, CompilerBuiltin, CompilerAlgebra and AnyType in compiler mode (`GraphRepository.java:125-128`, `:260-261`, `:320-321`; `compiler/WellKnownNames.java:114-126`). So an edit to one of those four `.fsi` files makes the whole library stale. Measured: a branch whose `CompilerLibrary.fsi` differed from the base rebuilt all five (6.6, 56.6, 23.7, 1.6 and 1.5 s, 90 s). After the api edit of the experiment above, CompilerAlgebra and CompilerSystem each rebuilt in 1.7 s on their next compile.
- A failed library compile writes nothing. A type error put in `CompilerLibrary.fss` failed in 8.5 s and changed no cache file. A program compiled and run after it got the old jar and printed `v2` without any warning. Once the error was fixed, compiling the component rebuilt it (24 s), and the program printed `v3`.
- A killed library compile: killed at 14 s and at 19 s it wrote nothing; killed at 22 s it had written the jar but not the `.tfs`. Either way the next compile of the component rebuilt it in full (24 s), because its `.tfs` was older than the source.

Walk: an edit to the body in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` (assert's message) showed on the next walk run, with no wipe. That run took 13.7 s and re-analysed FortressLibrary only (its `interpreter_cache` and `interpreter_parsed_cache` entries); the next took 3.7 s. Reverting it re-analysed FortressLibrary again (12.1 s). An api edit under walk was not tried. Its roots are FortressLibrary, FortressBuiltin and AnyType (`WellKnownNames.java:129-140`), so an edit to one of their `.fsi` files should make every walk entry stale. The rule in `repo-internals.md` to wipe after any library edit no longer holds for walk, at least for an edit to a body.

Java or Scala:

- `ant compileAll` deletes `default_repository/caches` whole before compiling: `compileAll` depends on `compileCommon`, which depends on `cleanCache` (`build.xml:539`, `:715`, `:356-360`). Its `depend` task with `closure="yes"` (`build.xml:717-720`) recompiles everything that depends on a changed class.
- On the seeded tree, one comment added to `interpreter/glue/prim/IntLiteral.java` cost 38.7 s, with javac recompiling 1,077 of 1,807 files and scalac all of its sources, against 82 s cold. With nothing changed it took 33 s.
- Right after it, a compiled program died with `NoSuchMethodError: … fortress.CompilerBuiltin.coerce_ZZ32(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntLiteral)`, which is the bootstrap stub of the FACTS entry. The library order (15.6, 57.7, 23.7, 1.7 and 1.6 s, 100 s) cured it.
- A syntax error failed at scalac in 6.6 s (`build.xml:558`), and the caches were already gone. After the fix, `ant compileAll` took 25.8 s, with javac compiling 1 file.

Which runs read `default_repository/caches`:

- Only `fortress compile`, `fortress run`, `junit.sh` (`fortress junit`) and a direct walk run read it.
- `harness-one.sh`, `checker-count/run.sh`, `distance/run.sh`, `count-run.sh`, `mg-run.sh`, `ant testFast` and `ant testSystem` each run with a private cache (`-Dfortress.caches` or `FORTRESS_CACHES`), so they need neither the library order nor a warm cache.
- `harness-one.sh` starts its walk from an empty cache each time. About 11 s of its 15 to 16 s for three small tests is analysing the library.

### The rules for a worker

After an edit:

- Edited `X.fss` of a library component, and not its `.fsi`: `fortress compile X.fss`, that component alone (CompilerBuiltin about 60 s, CompilerLibrary about 25 s, the others 2 to 16 s). Programs need no recompile.
- Edited the `.fsi` of AnyType, CompilerBuiltin, CompilerLibrary or CompilerAlgebra: all five in library order, about 100 s. Edited `CompilerSystem.fsi`: CompilerSystem alone.
- Compiling your own program never rebuilds the library. If you skip the step above, a body edit runs the old code with no warning, and an api edit dies with `NoSuchMethodError`.
- Walk needs nothing: it re-analyses an edited library source on its next run.
- Edited Java or Scala: run `ant compileAll` (25 to 40 s on a built tree), then `git checkout -- default_repository/caches/global.map`. Run the library order (about 100 s) only before a compiled run (`fortress compile`, `fortress run`, `junit.sh`). Harness-one, the checker count, the distance stage and the suites use their own caches and need neither.
- Do not wipe the cache for any of these.

After a failed build:

- `ant compileAll` failed: fix the error and run it again. The cache is already gone, because cleanCache runs first; there is nothing else to clear. Then restore `global.map`, and run the library order before any compiled run.
- `fortress compile` of a library component failed or was killed: it wrote nothing, or only its jar. Fix the error and compile that component again before any compiled run, because until then programs link its old jar without any warning. Delete nothing.
- A `NoSuchMethodError` from a compiled run means a component was not recompiled after an edit or after `ant compileAll`. Recompile the edited component, or run the library order. Do not wipe.

## 3. The script

`explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]`; its header gives the usage. It makes the worktree with the same `git worktree add` fallbacks as the shared prefix (`climb-batch-workflow.js:854`), or a detached one at the base when `<branch>` is `-`. It copies and translates as in section 1. It stamps library sources that differ from the base's commit, committed or not, later than the cache, and lists them, so that their next `fortress compile` rebuilds them. It warns when `ProjectFortress/src` differs from the base, since the copied build is then the base's.

It refuses an unbuilt or dirty base (exit 2, nothing made). It leaves alone a worktree that already has a build, so a relaunch keeps the worker's own build; `SEED_FORCE=1` replaces it. It reads the base and writes only the new worktree.

Shown working on a fresh worktree:

- A new branch `wip/seed-demo` cut from a local branch whose head adds a function to CompilerLibrary was seeded in 3 s. The script listed `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi` and `.fss` as newer than the cache.
- The library order then rebuilt all five (90 s, section 2). A program calling the new function compiled and printed `v1`.
- `harness-one.sh` on two tests gave `OK (2 tests)` and `junit.sh` on Compiled10.test gave `OK (3 tests)`, and `git status` was clean.
- A detached copy of the base was seeded in 3 s. The run against an existing worktree left it alone. An unbuilt base was refused with exit 2.

## 5. What the workflow can change

- At the launch: one base worktree from the batch's base. Run `ant compileAll`, restore `global.map`, run the library order and one passing walk test (for example `bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss`, which warms the walk caches), about 200 s.
- Each rung worktree: `seed-worktree.sh <base> <worktree> <branch>` in place of the shared prefix's compileAll and library order (`climb-batch-workflow.js:857`, `:868-877`). It costs 3 s and leaves the worktree warm for walk as well.
- A skeptic's or a repair's old-against-new run: `seed-worktree.sh <base> <worktree>-base -`, a private copy, so that two agents never compile into one cache. It replaces every `git checkout <base> -- ProjectFortress/src` and rebuild in the rung's own worktree.
- The prefix's text "cannot be warmed from the main tree" (`:868`) is true of a plain copy and false of a translated one. The worker's rules in section 2 can replace its paragraph on rebuilds (`:1033`).
- The gate after a repair runs again only when the repair changed `ProjectFortress/`, `Library/` or `build.xml`.

## For Pavol

Yes, the build can be shared. One finished build is copied into each new work tree in about 3 seconds, and the copy fixes the places where the folder's location is written into the saved results. Fortress accepts the copy and rebuilds nothing. Programs and tests give the same results as in the original, and the copy never reads the original's files. The 3 to 7 minutes each rung, skeptic and repair spent rebuilding goes away.

Fortress does notice edits, but only when you compile the part you edited: compiling your own program does not rebuild the library under it. If that step is skipped, the run either uses the old code without saying so or crashes with a missing-method error. A wipe is never the fix; recompiling the edited part is.

In batch 8, the four rungs each built the same starting point, and the skeptics and one repair rebuilt states the workers had already built. After the review's repair, which changed only specification text, the whole 25-minute gate ran again with the same result. That is about 107 minutes and 230K tokens of repeated work. One build at the launch, a copy per worktree, and skipping the gate when no code changed remove all of it.

## What a batch commits (2026-09-29)

A batch commits on a `wip/` branch what it commits on `main`, and nothing else: the Fortress change (source, library, specification text, tests), its reports (`REPORT.md`, `SKEPTIC.md`, `JUDGE.md` and a specification rung's `decision-record.md`, and the batch's `RECORD.md`), the ledger rows, the `FACTS.md` and `PLAN.md` lines, the handover line, and a script that is reusable. No captured output, log, raw output, probe program, copy of a script or test, list or dump is committed anywhere. An agent's scratch lives under `tmp/<slug>/` in its worktree, which `.gitignore:64` (`/tmp/`) ignores, and goes with the worktree when the commit stage removes it; the workers' transcripts, which the backup keeps, are the record of how a worker got where it did, and its test's failure before the fix is shown by its skeptic's own run, not by a file. The source is Pavol's decision of 2026-09-29 (`POSITIONS.md`, what a batch commits); the practice stage by stage is `postmortem-2026-09-29/synthesis.md`, section 1.

## Preparing a batch record

An Opus planning worker drafts `CLIMB-BATCH-<n>.md` and commits it. On Pavol's yes each time, one Fable worker then reviews it in place: it edits the record directly, writes one reason per change in a short review note (`climb-batch-6-review.md` is the example), and commits, so that the diff between the two versions shows exactly what the review changed. The coordinator reads that diff, fixes what is left, and brings the questions in section 1 to Pavol one per message; the batch launches on his go (batches 5 and 6; his words in the two entries of 2026-09-26 on the review of those manifests, in `POSITIONS-history.md`).

The planner builds each rung's briefing, writes it into the rung's section of the record, and the manifest carries it as the rung's `briefing` ("Shared prefix"). Its purpose is in-context learning (Pavol, 2026-09-27): the agents were not trained on Fortress, the language was never finished, and what they write from other languages' habits contradicts the specification and the library unless they have absorbed what the project has gathered. So a briefing carries, as keys of `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh`, decisions first: the `POSITIONS.md` entries, ledger rows and earlier judges' rulings the rung rests on; the specification's sections its subject touches, whole sections by their `\section` or `\subsection` heading and never grep hits; the probe and review notes already written on the subject, found through `INDEX.md`, by section; the library code that is the precedent for the same kind of problem, by the declarations it starts at; and the `FACTS.md` entries and map rows and sections of its area. Relevance decides what goes in, not size. The planner marks the sub-list the skeptic, the repair round and the judges read as `checks`: the decisions and ledger rows their checks need, and the specification's sections and the precedent code those checks compare against, for O the overflow subsections of `opr-overview.tex` and the glue natives it edits. Each list goes through `facts-extract.sh --check` on the tree the batch is cut from, every key matching exactly one place, and the tool's size line gives the reading it costs. Batch 6's four manifest entries are the worked examples, O's being the one batch 6b runs.

A record asks a rung for no corpus-wide output comparison, no ladder 'before', no microGPT check, no specification build log and no whole-suite run. The prefix allows one whole-suite run, at most once per code state in a rung's chain, and only to a rung whose edit changes the checker's or walk's source (Java or Scala under `ProjectFortress/src/`): the compiler and library tracks for the checker, the interpreter suite for walk. The worker runs it after its last edit, and a repair round after its own, with the verdict lines, command and commit in `REPORT.md`; the skeptic reads that result and does not run it again. Every other rung leaves the suites' verdict to the gate. A stop the record reserves that turns on a test's verdict (a verdict changed other than the rung's own, a set walk loaded refused after) is judged by the gate on the merged tree, and the record says so rather than asking a rung for a suite run (climb batch 7b's review, finding 5, approved 2026-09-30). In 7b rung C's chain ran the compiler and library tracks whole five times, twice on an unchanged tree, about 8 minutes of the box each, and found nothing its targeted runs had not. Rung W ran the interpreter suite once, because its record's verdict stops asked for what only a suite run shows. It asks for a measurement only where a test or a decision needs it, names it once for the whole batch when two rungs share a base, and states the one new thing it is for (protocol principle 5). A count of the programs a change reaches, when a decision needs one, is the planner's probe, taken before the record is written. A one-time count of changed interpreter outputs is asked for only where a decision of Pavol's names it for that rung (row 330's rung, and the numeral switch's Q-lib, rung Q of batch 8, whose measurement sits inside the rung), one edit pass against one base pass the coordinator starts before the launch; the record's section 7 holds no copy of the manifest, which `plan-<n>/manifest/` generates.

## Shared prefix

Since 2026-09-30 the rung worker makes its own worktree, and the coordinator makes none at the launch (climb batch 7b's review, finding 9). In 7b no worktree was made at the launch, where the script's header said it launched "after the worktrees exist". W and S found none and made their own, and L's first run searched the tree for how. The header now says the worker makes it. "Your worktree" gives the one command, with the base, and the worktree and branch from the rung's tail: `git -C /home/user/fortress fetch -q origin BRANCH 2>/dev/null ; [ -d WORKTREE ] || git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add WORKTREE BRANCH 2>/dev/null || git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add -b BRANCH WORKTREE <base>`, then the push of the branch. The command reuses a worktree that exists after a VM restart and a branch already pushed after a container death, and otherwise cuts the branch from the base; its three cases were run on a scratch repository. `ant compileAll` then runs in the new worktree before its first build or test. `ProjectFortress/build` is gitignored, and the analysed cache cannot be taken from the main tree, since its key hashes the source path; a symlinked build would point every cache path at the main tree (`batched-climb-review.md`, finding 2; FACTS, "The Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box", for the two agents at once). The paragraph that said the build "has been copied in" says so, and the worker's retry is told to make the worktree if it does not exist.

New: a `run_bg`/`wait_for` pair at five-second granularity (item 7); a worker's scratch goes under its worktree's `tmp/<slug>/` and is never committed (post-mortem 2026-09-29); `ant` is never piped through `tail` (item i). Since 2026-09-29 the same section says that an agent stops or kills only processes under its own worktree's path, never by a script's name across the box: in climb batch 6.5b rung V stopped its own corpus pass with `ps -eo pid,args | grep -E 'count-run.sh|…' | … | xargs -r kill`, which also killed rung E's two base passes, run under a copy of the same runner, and E recorded their end as "the cause was not found" (`reviews/batch-6.5b-review.md`, finding 4). Rule 2 asks for the site count when a precedent repaired a defect (item 6); rule 3 asks for the passage rather than the grep hit, ten lines either side (item 2). Rule 4's closing sentence, and the judge's `stop` question with it, named batch 3.5's two stops, a change to a declared type the prelude already has and a renamed or removed declaration a gated test uses, as if they applied to every batch; since 2026-09-26 both point to the stops the batch record's intro reserves for Pavol, at the head of the prefix (`open-items-2026-09-26.md`, item 27; batch 6's rung F changes declared types by Pavol's decisions). The register paragraph names a test by its topic and limits it to one comment line saying what it checks, with no pointer to a record (post-mortem 2026-09-29, section 2(c)). Since 2026-10-02 the re-anchoring rule for tests is gone (Pavol's yes of 2026-09-30; synthesis section 2(c)). Until then a rung that edited a specification chapter re-anchored, in its own commit, every `.tex` line its edit moved in the tests' messages and comments: batch 7b's rung S changed 49 test files and W 2, 310 lines in all. The one-time strip, `dc0eee2fe`, rewrote 823 specification citations in 139 test files to name the file and the section or entry. The rule in its place is in home 1's paragraph. A test cites the specification by its file and its section or entry by name, never by a line, and a new test does the same. A specification edit then moves no test's citation. What a citation is checked for is that the named section's text says what the message says: the skeptic's check 6. A rung that renames or removes a section a test names changes that citation in the commit of its edit, and that is the one test change a prose rung's skeptic allows (check 3). The rule stays in batch 7b's MANIFEST block, in its intro and rung S's tail, as 7b's record wrote it. The block is replaced whole at the next launch, so a record drafted for the next batch must not carry it. Since 2026-09-30 the paragraph after "Do NOT run ant testFast or ant testSystem" forbids a whole suite run any other way, except the one run per code state a checker or walk rung may make ("Preparing a batch record"), and the skeptic's closing paragraph has it read that run's result rather than run it again. "If your branch already carries commits" no longer tells a resumed worker to "re-run its checks rather than trusting its logs": a check whose log is complete stands unless the tree changed after it, and only a log cut off or failed is a step still to do. After 7b's VM restart, rung C's second run ran the compiler and library tracks and the distance stage again on a tree whose results were complete on disk, about 25 minutes of the box, because that sentence asked for it (`reviews/batch-7b-review.md`, finding 5).

"Your briefing", added 2026-09-27 before the territory map, says what a briefing holds and who reads which part of it, and names no rung, so the prefix stays byte-identical across the batch's agents. Each role on a rung runs `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh` once, as its first step, with keys from the rung's manifest entry: the rung worker, and a worker resumed after a stop, read the whole `briefing`; the skeptic, the repair round after a refusal and the judge read its `checks` sub-list, and the judges and the repair on the merged tree read every rung's `checks`. The tool prints each key's entry whole and in the order given: a `POSITIONS.md` entry by `positions:DATE WORDS` (the entry of that date whose head, its text up to the first colon and space, holds the words; from `POSITIONS-history.md`, saying so, when `POSITIONS.md` has none), a ledger row by `ledger:ROW`, a judge's ruling, a note's section or a specification section by `doc:PATH#HEADING` (in a `.tex` or `.tick` file the headings are its sectioning commands, macros dropped; a heading equal to the key wins over the ones that hold it, and `A > B` names B's section inside A's), a map section by `map:FILE#HEADING`, one table row, list item or bold-lead paragraph of a section by `@WORDS`, code by `code:PATH#FROM..TO` (from the declaration on the one line holding FROM through the end of the one at the next line holding TO, braces counted in Java and Scala, indentation and `end` in Fortress, with line numbers), a `FACTS.md` entry by its title and `INDEX.md` lines by `index:`. It prints in parts of at most 28 KB, under the 30,000 characters one shell command shows an agent, with `--part N` to continue, and opens with the size of the whole output in bytes and estimated tokens (0.41 a byte and 110 a part, the rate `explorations/reviews/worker-context-cost.md` fitted); `--check` prints where each key matches and its size, and `--root DIR` reads another checkout's record. The script refuses a key holding a double quote, a backtick, a dollar sign or a backslash, since each is rendered in double quotes, and a `checks` key missing from `briefing`. Until this change every such role also ran `--common`, the map README's three sections, `PLAN.md`'s phases and `repo-internals.md` whole, the same for every agent; no role runs it now. Pavol's reasons, 2026-09-27: the early climbs failed on agents' local decisions, and the record exists so that an agent works from the whole territory; and the briefing is in-context learning, since the agents were never trained on Fortress ("Preparing a batch record"). The reason for its shape is two reviews of that day: the misses of the later batches sat in ledger rows, `POSITIONS.md` entries, earlier judges' rulings and the library's own precedents, which neither `FACTS.md` nor the maps carry (`explorations/reviews/worker-global-decisions.md`); and a 29K-token read first, half of it `--common`, priced over the 78 agents measured, would have cost more than the gathering it could remove: on rung workers the cost fell inside the range it could save, and on skeptics and repairs it was a cost in every case (`explorations/reviews/worker-context-cost.md`).

"What a measured defect is worth" is the rule that closes the 22-and-2 gap. Every defect anyone measures has one of three homes and the record says which:

1. **repaired in the rung**, whoever measured it → an assertion in the rung's own gated test, passing before the second skeptic runs (item a);
2. **deferred, specification settles it** → a gated expected-failure test named `XXX…` asserting the specification's answer. The mechanism is cited so it can be checked: `FileTests.java:932` sets `shouldFail` from the name and `:587`/`:654` make `shouldFail != failed` the failure condition, so the suite goes red the day the test starts passing; `:851` names the case and the author's warning at `:853` is why a rung's first `XXX` file is shown to go red on a deliberate local fix (item b). Since 2026-09-29 the paragraph also carries the line that decides a run test, and two sentences with it (`reviews/batch-6.5b-review.md`, finding 1 and measure 1). In `compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` an unmet `run_out_*` check fails a run test before the flag is read (`:534-539`, `:583-585`, before `:587`), and a run test with no such check demands `PASS` (`:276-282`); so an `XXX` run test's key names output the failing run does print before it dies, `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` where it dies before any output, never `run_out_contains=PASS`, citing the two `FACTS.md` entries on the mechanism. The first `XXX` file is shown through the harness itself, placed where the gate reads it and on the fix (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh`; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh` for `tests/`), not only by a direct compile and run. And a program the checker accepts that then fails JVM verification, linkage or a range check at run time is home 2, never 3 (`reviews/batch-N-review.md`, measure 6, which had not been built). The reason: climb batch 6.5b's rung V keyed its `XXX` run test on `PASS`, and it and its skeptic showed the red by a direct run, as the paragraph then allowed, citing exactly `:932`, `:587` and `:654`; only a briefing that carried the `FACTS.md` entry saw the rule, and in batch 7b one of four did. The gate went red on it, and the red cost 79 minutes and 1.2M tokens, a fifth of the run;
3. **deferred, specification silent** → a test pinning today's behaviour and a ledger row; where no program can observe it, the ledger row alone, quoting the output (post-mortem 2026-09-29).

A home-2 test is owed in the batch that measures the defect, even when a later rung or batch is planned to repair it; the argument that it can wait for the repairing rung was ruled against three times (batches 6b, 7R and 7C; `reviews/batch-7C-review.md`, the repeat; `reviews/process-review-6b-7-7R.md`, measure 3). The rule text the agents read carries the same sentence.

A report cites the Fortress tree and quotes its results; the tracked-path check is gone with the captures (post-mortem 2026-09-29).

"If your context is compacted", added 2026-09-29, tells every agent of the batch that its brief is the first message of its own transcript (the newest `agent-*.jsonl` under `~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/workflows/` whose first line holds the prefix's title and its role's heading), to re-read from it and from the files it wrote what its next step needs, and that the boot CLAUDE.md asks for after a compaction, the coordinator's `README.md`, the protocol, `FACTS.md` and `POSITIONS.md`, is the coordinator's, as is the coordinator's session transcript. Batch N's gather ran that boot and searched the coordinator's transcript after its compaction, about 45K of its 70K tokens of re-orientation (`reviews/batch-N-review.md`, question 1; "Rules weighed by what they cost", below).

## Rung worker

Step 1 is the rung's whole briefing ("Shared prefix"), put to the worker as a mission briefing: it works in a language it was not trained on, learns from the briefing how Fortress does things, and then does the rung in the library's own way with the ledger and the decisions on record in mind, looking in the same places where the rung goes past the briefing; and the steps after it moved down by one on 2026-09-27; a worker resumed after the judge rules that its stop is not one reads the whole briefing too, and a repair round after a refusal reads the `checks` sub-list. Step 2 fixes the check line at `run_out_contains=PASS` and notes that `run_out_WIcontains` is now implemented rather than silently inert (item d). Step 9 is the three-homes obligation. The provenance block gains a fifth line, `historical:`, naming every 2012-tree file the rung edits (item 8, the protocol's hard rule on the gate). `RUNG_SCHEMA` gains `historicalFiles` and `defectHomes`. Since the post-mortem of 2026-09-29 the worker's first commit on its branch is the test alone, seen failing through the harness; its scratch is under the worktree's `tmp/<slug>/` and is never committed; the ladder subset runs after the edit only; no rung runs a corpus comparison or a microGPT check; `wait_for` polls at 270 s. A rung that edits only the specification or other prose, where no test can go red (a prose edit of `Specification/` or `Documentation/`, which moves no test's citation, since tests name the section and not the line), makes no test-only commit and has no failure to see: steps 2, 3 and 6 do not apply, its skeptic checks its text against the tree and the decisions on record instead, and it commits no build log, capture or PDF, the PDF being the commit stage's (`postmortem-2026-09-29/script-review.md`, finding 2). A `testIsStage` rung's step 3 runs once steps 4 and 5, the edit and its rebuild, are done (`postmortem-2026-09-29/script-review.md`, finding 10). The tracked-path check, step 12 until then, and its `trackedPaths` field went with the captures.

Since 2026-09-26 it also carries `reportText` and `recordText`, the full text of `REPORT.md` and `record.md` word for word, and `stopsMet`, which is required. In batch 5 the harness refused the rung workers' writes of `REPORT.md`, and the gather composed each report from the structured result, whose `summary` is at most 15 lines (`CLIMB-BATCH-6.md` section 8, item 1); in batch N it refused all four. Since 2026-09-29 the gather writes a missing file from these fields as the run's journal holds them, not from its brief ("Rules weighed by what they cost", below). `stopsMet` lists every stop the batch record's intro reserves for Pavol that the rung met, including one met on part of the work while the rest lands. Each entry has the stop, its evidence and `liftedBy`, which is the `POSITIONS.md` line of the decision of Pavol's that lifts it, or empty. The skeptic and the merged-diff review return the same field (`STOPS_MET`), and the commit stage reads all three (below).

Each rung's worker commits and pushes to its own `wip/<slug>` branch as it works, so a dead container loses nothing; the gather composes one commit per rung on `main`.

`RUNG_SCHEMA` also gains `forPavol`, every point for Pavol the rung does not settle, one entry each with its evidence: a decision taken inside the rung on a question that was his, a fork, a defect or divergence that lands unrepaired and needs his word (the reports the tail's "What comes back to Pavol" names reach him with the landing and are not such points). A repair round carries in `forPavol` every point the rung still has, the earlier pass's included, since the script reads the last worker's list.

## Skeptic

Check 1 is the `checks` sub-list of the rung's briefing ("Shared prefix"); the checks after it, numbered from 0 until 2026-09-27, moved down by two. Check 9 is the three homes — the skeptic runs the test itself to see a home-1 assertion pass. Check 3 is the failure seen by the skeptic itself: the test run on the worker's test-only commit and at the branch's head, rebuilt at each, the skeptic's own programs and its commit on the branch again (`postmortem-2026-09-29/script-review.md`, finding 11); for a rung that edits only prose, the text checked against the tree and the decisions on record, with no refusal for a failure no test can show (`postmortem-2026-09-29/script-review.md`, finding 2). Check 2 covers the fifth provenance line. The manifest's `expectedCheckerCount` is written beside the two as a prediction, not a value the table must meet. W's skeptic could not check the provenance block, and the skeptics of C, S and L searched the run's transcripts for the text. The script cannot see the branch, so it passes the text whenever the worker returned one. The line says that where the branch carries the file, the file is the report and this is its copy; where it does not, the text is the report, and the checks of `REPORT.md` are checks of it. It costs the report's size on every first and second skeptic, 27 to 59 KB in batch 7b, and duplicates the file where the write went through. `recordText` stays out: the skeptic reads `record.md` for check 8 only, and the gather writes it from the journal.

## Gather

Rungs are applied in ascending order of lowest edited line in the shared files, and a cited `file:line` that an earlier applied rung shifted is re-anchored by symbol (item 5). #!/bin/bash
# The distance stage's comparison: this table (run.sh's) against the last landed one.
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh <last-landed-table|""> <this-table>
#
# Prints one verdict line, then every #kind and #class row whose count moved, with the
# change, and every #crash row that went or came. It is REPORTED and never red: it always
# exits 0, whatever moved, a stale shadow and a run that produced no table included (Pavol,
# answer 11, POSITIONS.md 2026-09-26: a report-only stage, whose job is driving the distance
# down). The verdicts:
#   DISTANCE DOWN|UP|SAME   <last> -> <now>
#   DISTANCE FIRST          no landed table to compare with
#   DISTANCE NO TABLE       this run produced no count, with the table's own reason
#   SETTING CHANGED         the two tables ran different settings: the counts are not like for like
#   SHADOW STALE            a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources
# A move of 2 to 4 errors in the components' type errors or in which pair of LEXICO, SQCAP or
# INVERSE declarations an overloading error names is the checker's run-to-run variation
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md section 5), not a change; a crash row whose line numbers
# moved because a rung edited above it prints as one gone and one new.
set -u
OLD=${1:-}; NEW=${2:?usage: compare.sh <last-landed-table> <this-table>}
field () { awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '$1 == t { sub("^[^\t]*\t", ""); print; exit }' "$2" ; }

now=$(field '#total' "$NEW")
sh=$(field '#shadow' "$NEW")

A rung whose manifest entry sets `testIsStage` has that stage as its test. The before is the last landed gate's table (POSITIONS 2026-09-28); step 3 of the order of work runs the stage once after the edit and its rebuild, to the worktree's `tmp/`, and the skeptic re-runs it, in place of the `.fss` component and its `.test` file; the skeptic's check 3 checks the report's diff against the two tables and re-runs the stage itself to see the post-edit one come out again, and check 6 checks the two tables differ in the way the report says. Nothing else about such a rung changes — the ladder subset, the three homes and the provenance block all stand. This is the one place the test-first rule is met by a permanent stage instead of a test file, and the reason is that no program can yet be compiled against the interpreter's prelude (`library-route-judgement.md` § 2 step 1, which also sets the stop condition: two runs printing the same table). The first rung of the library route is the rung this flag exists for.


## A repair of tests and records only (2026-09-29)

After a repair on the merged tree, the review's or the gate's, the whole gate runs again only when the repair, or the review's corrections, changed a path outside `explorations/` that is not a test file: source, library, checker, interpreter or specification (POSITIONS 2026-09-29, on rerunning the gate after a repair that only added tests; batch N's review repair added six compiler test files, run in the harness by the repair itself, and the batch waited on a whole gate for them). A test file is a `.fss`, `.fsi` or `.test` file directly in `ProjectFortress/tests/` or a `ProjectFortress/*_tests/` directory. The repair returns `headBefore`, `headAfter` and `pathsChanged`, and in `testRuns` each test file it added or changed, run in the harness on the merged tree with the gate's own JUnit mechanics, the files of one corpus together in one harness run, one JVM (below, "Rules weighed by what they cost", item 6; batch N's repair ran each in its own JVM, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/repair-junit-placed.txt`): `ONE_JVM=1 junit.sh` beside that capture for the `.test` files of `compiler_tests/`, and again for those of `library_tests/`, `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh` once for the interpreter tests; each file with its suite row, JUnit cases, verdict (that of the run that held it) and capture. `repairRerun` in the script decides. The gate runs again, as before, on a code path, a changed test no passing run exercises, a run that failed, or a repair that listed nothing; no second review follows it since the post-mortem of 2026-09-29, and the runs' captures stay under `tmp/gate-batch-<N>/`, not committed. After the gate's repair it also runs again unless every line the gate was red on is answered by a passing run (`failingAnswered`) and no suite count fell. Otherwise the first gate's tables stand, and the commit stage appends the runs to its `summary.txt` as `# repair-tests` lines, with their total: the next batch's gate counts rise beyond the summary's rows by those cases, and `gate_compare` skips `#` lines. When a later gate does run, the repair's tests are among its counts and no such lines are written. The script's stubbed check runs both kinds of repair through it: `compile-ladder/plan-n/manifest/checkn.js`, eight merged-tree scenarios, until the cleaning removed it from the tree at `ab067d9b6`; since 2026-09-30, `coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js`, scenarios R5, A7 to A9 and A14 ("Measured, and not", below).

Since 2026-09-29 the same rule reaches one stage earlier, extending Pavol's rule on rerunning the gate after a repair that only added tests (`reviews/batch-6.5b-review.md`, finding 2 and measure 2). When the gate that ran beside the review is red, and the review's corrections left it standing, the review's repair is given the gate's failing lines (`repairTestsStep`) and returns `failingAnswered` for them, answering a line only where its own ruling's edit is to the test the line names and its harness run passes it. After a repair of tests and records only, `repairRerun` is asked again with that gate; when every line is answered and no suite count fell, no gate judge and no gate repair run, and the commit records the runs and the answered lines beside the gate's summary, as after a gate's repair. A line the repair does not answer, a repair that changed code, and a review whose judge rules land take the paths they took before. The reason: in climb batch 6.5b the review's repair had fixed the one `.test` line the gate was red on and run the pair through the harness, placed and on the fix, yet the script passed its runs as answering nothing (`answered: []`) and sent the red gate to a gate judge, which ruled that the repair was already on `main`, and to a gate repair that ran the same pair again: 42 minutes, 30 of them the judge's wait on a permission prompt, and 0.38M tokens with a top-tier ruling.

## Before the launch

Besides what the batch record lists under its own "Before the launch.", the coordinator makes the batch's one base build (since 2026-10-02; POSITIONS, "Nothing is built or run twice on the same code."; `coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md`, section 5). It is a worktree at the batch's base, the commit passed as `args.base`, built once and then left alone: every rung worktree is seeded from it, and so is each rung's private copy of the base, and nobody compiles or runs anything in it. About 200 s, at a path outside the main tree, for example `/home/user/fortress-base<N>`:

    git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add --detach /home/user/fortress-base<N> <base>
    cd /home/user/fortress-base<N> && source explorations/experiment/env.sh && mkdir -p tmp
    ant compileAll > tmp/compileAll.txt 2>&1; tail -3 tmp/compileAll.txt    # BUILD SUCCESSFUL, about 80 s
    git checkout -- default_repository/caches/global.map                    # compileAll deletes the caches, this tracked file with them
    cd ProjectFortress && for c in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin ../Library/CompilerLibrary ../Library/CompilerAlgebra ../Library/CompilerSystem; do ../bin/fortress compile $c.fss || break; done; cd ..    # about 110 s
    bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss                       # one passing walk test, which warms the walk caches
    git status --porcelain                                                  # empty: seed-worktree.sh refuses a base that is not clean

Its path goes to the launch as `args.baseBuild`, beside `args.base`; the script refuses to start without it (scenario B1). One trial seed proves it before the launch, about 3 s: `explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck - <base>`, then `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree remove /home/user/fortress-seedcheck`. The disk read against the batch counts the base build and two seeded trees per rung, the rung's worktree and its copy of the base, about 206 MB each. The commit stage removes the rungs' copies with their worktrees; the base build stays until the coordinator removes it after the landing (`git -C /home/user/fortress worktree remove /home/user/fortress-base<N>`).

## Climb batch 9: one base build, and a skeptic that reads (2026-10-02)

Pavol decided on 2026-10-02 that the skeptic checks that the test-first procedure was followed and does not repeat it, and that nothing is built or run twice on the same code (POSITIONS, "Test first, the test kept.", its last sentence, and "Nothing is built or run twice on the same code.": "We don't want to re be rebuilding stuff that doesn't need to be rebuilt."). He took four changes of the skeptic-scope judgement (`coordinator/skeptic-scope-judgement.md`, section 5, items 1 to 4) and the build and cache exploration's proposals (`coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md`, section 5). The before is climb batch 8: 35 builds, 22 of them of a code state another agent had already built, about 85 minutes of the machine; a second whole gate after a repair of one sentence of the specification; the second skeptics' repeated list; about 0.5M written and an hour of the critical path in all (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 4; the exploration's section 4 puts the repeated work at 107 minutes and 230K tokens).

- **One base build, and every worktree seeded from it.** The coordinator builds one worktree at the base before the launch ("Before the launch", above), named by `args.baseBuild`. The prefix's "Your worktree" makes the rung's worktree with `tools/seed-worktree.sh <base build> WORKTREE BRANCH <base>`, which adds it with the same fallbacks as the old command and copies the base build's `ProjectFortress/build` and `default_repository/caches` with their path keys translated, in about 3 s, in place of `ant compileAll` and the library order in each worktree (the exploration, sections 1 and 3). If the seed exits 2, the worker makes the worktree and builds it itself, as before, and says so. I tried them on batch 8's transcripts: a worker's listing is 30 to 61 lines, and rung I's shows base run 13:10, test-only commit 13:13:16, first build of the edit 13:13:23.
   - A `testIsStage` skeptic now runs neither the count nor the distance stage. The judgement wanted to keep the 20-second count run; POSITIONS "Nothing is built or run twice" rules it out too, so I took it out.
   - Check 9 reads the home-1 assertion in the worker's passing run. The differential keeps its purpose, plus one sentence on where its old side runs.
2. **Second skeptic.** It has its own brief, `secondSkepticRole` :1242, called at :2489. It carries:
   - its first verdict and the judge's ruling;
   - the repair's structured result, plus its commits and diff since the refused head. The head comes from a new required `judgedHead` (schema :1506); if that is missing, the brief falls back to the parent of the commit that added SKEPTIC.md. SKEPTIC.md and JUDGE.md are left out of the diff.
   - the repair round's transcript;
   - the one question: does the repair answer the refusal without breaking what the first judgement approved.

   It may re-run its own programs and write new ones; nothing else from the first list. It writes "# Second judgement" at the top of SKEPTIC.md.
3. **The judgement's three small fixes:**
   - **Distance stage:** no skeptic re-runs it; check 3 now reads the worker's table with `compare.sh` (:1188, the stage branch).
   - **`skepticText`:** it is the word `committed` once the commit is made, with the text carried only when the write was refused, and no read-back (end of :1159's function; schema; recovery). The gather deletes a journal-written SKEPTIC.md that holds only that word and reports it missing (:1569).
   - **Record paragraph:** the skeptic's brief carries the rung's "For the skeptic" paragraph from the tail, and checks 6, 10 and 12 point to it. The prefix's sentence at :851 now says which part of the record each role's brief carries.
4. **Seeding (your a/b/c)** is in the shared prefix:
   - Worktrees are made with `seed-worktree.sh <BASE_BUILD> WORKTREE BRANCH <base>` (:867). If the seed exits 2, the worker falls back to making and building the worktree itself.

5. **Gate after a repair (d).** It reruns only for a path under `ProjectFortress/` that is not a test file, under `Library/`, or `build.xml` (`gateReads` :1952, `repairRerun` :2135). The review's own corrections follow the same rule (:2645). Other paths, such as `Specification/`, are recorded by `besideStep` (:2024) as `# repair-ungated` lines in summary.txt. The commit stage now also removes each rung's `<path>-base` copy (:2090).
6. **Manual.** New sections "Before the launch" (md :28) and "Climb batch 9: one base build, and a skeptic that reads" (:42), which cite the two POSITIONS entries, the judgement, the exploration and batch 8's review. The rebuild lines from script-review finding 11 are removed, the stale skeptic re-run sentences are corrected, and a checks paragraph is added (:244).

**Checks**
- `node --check` and the harness parse (`new AsyncFunction` with the export made `const`) both pass.
- `workflow-scenarios.js`: 34 scenarios, 0 problems. New ones:
  - S1: the second skeptic gets the short brief.
  - D1 and D4: a specification-only change, by a repair or by the review's own correction, gets no second gate and a step 1a record.
  - D2 and D3: a `Library/` or `build.xml` change reruns the gate.
  - B1: the script will not start without `baseBuild`.

  Every skeptic brief is checked for no `ant ` as a word, no rebuild, no checkout/switch/stash/reset and no `worktree add`; the record's own "For the skeptic" paragraph is excluded from that check. Against the script before this change, 32 of the 34 scenarios fail (1,037 problems).
- The grep `compileAll\|rebuild\|git checkout` over the skeptic's role text finds one line, :1119. It is the jq filter that lists the worker's builds in its transcript; it doesn't ask the skeptic to build.

**New launch argument and what you need to do before the launch**
- Launch with `args: {base: '<base>', baseBuild: '/home/user/fortress-base<N>'}`. The script throws without `baseBuild`.
- Make and build the base worktree at the exact base; the commands are in the manual's "Before the launch". It takes about 200 s:
  - `git worktree add --detach`
  - `ant compileAll`
  - `git checkout -- default_repository/caches/global.map`
  - the five library-order compiles
  - one walk test (`bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss`)
  - check `git status --porcelain` is empty
- Optionally run one trial seed to a scratch path and remove it.
- Disk: about 206 MB per seeded tree, two per rung plus the base build.
- Nobody may compile or run in the base build, or the seed refuses it as not clean.
- The batch-9 record's Launch line still shows `args: {base}`, so it needs `baseBuild` added. Its "What a worker clears…" line is now covered by the script.
- You remove the base build after the landing; the commit stage removes only the rung copies.

**Not in this change, though CLIMB-BATCH-9.md section 8 lists them:**
- item 2: add `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/` to `STAGE_BLIND`;
- item 4's move of check 8 to the review's check 3 (the record cites judgement items 3–5, while my brief named items 2–4);
- item 6: cap `wait_for`'s bound at 270 s.

One existing gap remains: if the first skeptic commits SKEPTIC.md but the harness refuses the second skeptic's write, the gather never runs its journal command, because the file exists, and the second judgement's text is lost.

Other workers have uncommitted edits to `CLIMB-BATCH-9.md` and `plan-9/manifest/gen9.py` in the main tree; I didn't touch them.
